【3】**PHYSICAL AND NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION**

【4】Prior to the physical and neurological examination the psychiatrist will conduct a comprehensive review of systems； previous and ongoing medical problems need to be identified. The patient’s prenatal， perinatal， and developmental histo-ries are relevant. History of seizures， head trauma， fractures， and prior surgeries will be noted. In females， menarche， menstrual cycle， and any pregnancy history are pertinent. History ofalcohol or drug abuse is also of particular importance. For both sexes， history ofsexual behavior， contraception， andSTDs is relevant. Any history of physical or sexual abuse must be obtained.

【5】The psychiatric assessment is enriched when the psychiatrist conducts the physical and neurological examinations. The examiner will seek evidence of dysmorphic features compatible with 22q11 syndrome. It is advisable to have a parental figure accompaning the child or adolescent during the examination， especially if the child is a female. Rectal and genital examinations are deferred to the primary care physician or to specialists when indicated. When there are indications of sexual abuse or of rape， the child will be referred for a forensic examination. Rape crisis evaluations， specially designated for this objective， provide developmentally sensitive examinations for small children. These diagnostic and treatment centers are available in designated medical-surgical hospitals across the nation.

【6】For most female patients， and for children in general， the performance of the physical and neurological examination (even when is done by the psychia-trist) is an uneventful experience without any detrimental side effects. These examinations pose no significant risks for the building of a therapeutic alliance with the psychiatrist .

【7】When the psychiatrist performs the physical examination， he or she will pay attention to the child's relatedness and the degree of the childs participation dur-ing the examination. The presence of dysmorphic features or of facial features suggestive of identifiable syndromes should be noted (i.e.， facial features sug-gestive of chromosome 22q11 delesion syndrome， or velocardiofacial syndrome(VCFS) may clarify the clinical presentation； see chapter 8， pp. 207-208).

**Minor physical anomalies (MPAs) and dermatoglyphic abnormalities are associated with risks for schizophrenia. A Danish study found that children|删除0换行|(11-13 years ofage) with MPAs were more likely to go on to develop schizophre-nia spectrum disorders in adulthood. MPAs are more frequent in children with early onset schizophrenia (EOS). For a subset ofthese patients who underwent MRI examaination，the MPA scores were positively correlated with ventricular enlargement .

【9】Reassurance and a greater sensitivity should be exercised during the physi-cal evaluation of a psychotic child. Explaining to the child what the examina-tion entails and describing to the patient what the physician is about to do is helpful in lessening anxieties and dispelling apprehensions. During the examination， the physician will have the opportunity to notice the degree of the patient’s cooperation and orientation to reality. The physician should pay attention to other valuable observations such as the degree and appro-priateness of the child’s relatedness， evidence of suspiciousness or paranoia， disturbances of reality testing， signs of anxiety， or evidence of drug abuse. The physician will observe the degree of the child's neglect to his body (poor oral and body hygiene， untreated skin infections， unclipped finger or toenails， ingrown toenails， and others).

【10】The patient's complexion， baseline weight， and vital signs will be registered. RR6egularity ofthe pulse will be noted. Any evidence ofinjury needs to be inves-tigated. Signs of self-abusive behavior should be noted and addressed in further interviewing， as should evidence of substance abuse， obesity， or cachexia. The physician will assess the thyroid size， its firmness and its regularity.

【11】Acanthosis nigricans and o OS1Sther cutaneous and neurocutaneous findings should be pursued with further inquiry， testing， or consultation referrals. The evaluation of the cardiorespiratory systems is particularly pertinent. When the patient has a history of fainting or blacking out， a history of shortness of breath or exercise dyspnea， further investigation is mandatory. The presence of rhythm dificulties， murmurs， or any other cardiovascular finding will be noted； these require further testing and consultation. It is prudent to assume that every obese child has cardiomegaly requiring a pediatric cardiologic consultation. Any ongoing illness or medical-surgical condition will be ap-propriately attended to.

【12】In the neurological examination， the physician will make observations on the patients degree of alertness， orientation to time and place， and his or her sense of boundaries. Attention should be given to the quality oflanguage and melody of speech (prosody)， as well as the child's affective display. Fun-doscopy should be performed on every child； the physician will identify the presence of cranial nerve signs， deficits in the gross or fine motor movements， abnormal reflexes， or difficulties with praxis or coordination. Problems with right to left differentiation， finger sequencing difficulties， or difficulties with bimanual behavior may also shed some light in the childs neurodevelopmental problems； such is the case of language deficits， learning disorders， and cogni-tive deficits.

【13】In addition to the above observations， testing may reveal neurological abnormalities， apparently specific to schizophrenia， that indicate neurological compromise in the left heteromodal association cortex and cerebellum. Motor abnormalities are common in schizoprenia and in nonschizoprenic psychosis， and correlate with cerebellum and straital abormalities， but with limited in-volvement of the heteromodal area . A bedside neurological evaluation derived from the Neurological Evaluation scale may assist in the differential diagnosis . Items that particularly correlate with a decrease in heteromodal association cortex and cerebellum volume in schizophrenia are：

【15】·NES， item 13， Memory. The patient is told four words and he is asked to repeat the words immediately after they are presented. The subject is asked to recall the words again 5 and 10 minutes later.

【16】· NES， item 18，Extinction (Face-Hand test)： the subject， with his eyes closed， is simultaneouly touched in the following order： right cheek-left hand，left cheek-right hand， right cheek-right hand， and left cheek-left hand. The patient needs to identify where he was touched. For a complete review of the NES testing items and their scoring， see Buchanan and Heinrichs.

【19】Soft neurological signs， frequently found in chronic psychotic patients， are not stable findings； they change with the state of the illness. Soft neurological signs decreased in first-episode adult schizophrenic patients at a follow-up period of 14 monthss. This effect was related to better outcome. Despite the improvement， soft signs remained elevated in schizophrenic patients relative to heathy controls. Findings are in harmony with the concept that neurological soft signs range among the most consistent neurobiological characteristics of schizophrenia. Patients with decreasing soft signs scores experienced further stabilization of psychiatric symptoms， whereas patients with stable scores fore-shadowed a chronic course .

【17】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【18】 Atrial septal defect (ASD): The presence of shunt vascularity and right-sided cardiac enlargement along with reported cardiac murmur on exam are most suggestive of this diagnosis.

【19】 Ventricular septal defect (VSD): With this diagnosis you would see shunt vascularity and right heart enlargement, but would also expect left-sided cardiac enlargement. In addition, VSDs almost always present at a younger age.

【20】 Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVR): This may also result in shunt vascularity and right-sided cardiac enlargement. Occasionally, there is radiographic evidence of an anomalous vein draining the right upper lobe into the SVC or the left upper lobe into a vertical vein.

【21】 Primary pulmonary hypertension: Can cause progressive shortness of breath in a young female with resulting pulmonary artery and right-sided cardiac enlargement if severe. However, would expect enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries with more distal tapering.

【22】DIAGNOSIS

【23】Atrial septal defect—ostium secundum/fossa ovalis type

【24】KEY FACTS

【25】Clinical

【26】 ASD is a common congenital heart disease. It represents approximately 30% of congenital heart disease in adults.

【27】 Possible complications arising in individuals with ASDs include right ventricular volume overload, pulmonary hypertension, atrial fibrillation, rarely paradoxical embolism, and even progression to Eisenmenger’s syndrome if left untreated.

【28】 The development of the interatrial septum is a multistep coordinated process. The three most common lesions that result from failure of normal septal development are

【29】>  Ostium primum defect—occurs in the region of the fossa primum, at the caudal aspect of the septum primum and secundum, most often caused by or concomitant with nonfusion of the medial AV cushions.

【30】>  Ostium secundum/fossa ovalis defect—most common defect. Occurs due to resorption of the septum primum or incomplete formation of the septum secundum.

【31】>  Sinus venosus ASD—defect in the region of the normal fossa secundum due to lack of formation or reabsorption of the adjacent septum secundum. This defect occurs near the superior vena cava entrance to the right atrium and is associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.

【32】 Treatment of an ASD depends on the size, location, and degree of symptoms. If the defect is small, closure can be attempted via transcatheter occlusion device. Larger and more complicated defects may require open surgical correction.

【33】Radiologic

【34】 Radiographic findings of ASD include shunt vascularity, right atrial enlargement, and right ventricular enlargement.

【35】 MR evaluation includes T1-weighted and cine gradient-echo sequences often performed in short-axis and four-chamber views as well as orthogonal to the septal defect. MR angiography is also commonly performed.

【36】 On MR and CT, the thin fossa ovalis may be mistaken for an ASD. On MR, the ASD must be seen on two contiguous slices and be confirmed by a flow jet on cine MR images.

【37】 Velocity-encoding MR may be used to estimate the pulmonary to systemic flow gradient (Qp/Qs) which, if >1, can indicate the hemodynamic significance of the defect.

【38】 CTA may be useful in evaluation if cardiac gating is utilized and fine cuts (slice thickness of 1.25 mm or below) are obtained, although the functional significance of the defect is better assessed with MR.

【39】 Evaluation with MR can be useful in evaluating the coronary and cardiac anatomy, the present of Eisen-menger’s physiology, and myocardial viability in a patient under consideration for correction of ASD.

【56】KEY FACTS

【57】Clinical

【58】 There are two common forms of right aortic arches: right arch with mirror image branching and right aortic arch with an aberrant left subclavian artery.

【59】 Right aortic arch with mirror image branching (first branch is left innominate artery; second branch is right common carotid artery; third branch is right subclavian artery) is strongly associated (95% to 98%) with congenital heart disease. Tetrology of Fallot (TOF) is the most common association, and truncus arteriosus is the second most common.

【60】 Right aortic arch with ALSA (first branch is left common carotid artery; second branch is right common carotid artery; third branch is right subclavian artery; fourth branch is aberrant left subclavian artery) is only associated with congenital heart disease in approximately 5% patients. In those patients who do have congenital heart disease in association with an aberrant left subclavian type of right arch, TOF is the most common associated entity.

【61】 The aberrant left subclavian artery usually arises off of a diverticulum (the diverticulum of Kommerell). The aberrant subclavian artery then courses posterior to both the trachea and the esophagus to reach the left arm.

【62】 Right aortic arches are a form of complete vascular ring, with a left ligamentum arteriosum completing the vascular ring.

【63】 Patients with a mirror image type of right aortic arch usually present as a result of their associated congenital heart disease. Rarely, patients have respiratory symptoms as a result of tracheal compression from the vascular ring.

【64】 Older patients with a right aortic arch and ALSA may develop an aneurysm of the left subclavian artery, resulting in esophageal compression and dysphagia lusoria.

【65】Radiological

【66】 Presence of a right aortic arch is most accurately determined by tracheal deviation to the left on the frontal radiograph. There will be no tracheal deviation to the right, as would be expected if there was a left-sided transverse aorta.

【67】 The diverticulum of Kommerell results in anterior deviation of the tracheal air column (and the esophagus) on the lateral view. Frequently, there will be a prominent soft tissue density in the retrotracheal region, just posterior to the area of tracheal deviation.

【68】 On the frontal film, the diverticulum of Kommerell may cause a slight left mediastinal contour abnormality, but will not impress on the left tracheal wall.

【69】 Right aortic arches usually descend on the right. However, this is variable, particularly in older patients in whom the descending aorta may be tortuous.

【70】 The radiograph should be inspected for signs of associated congenital heart disease, particularly TOF: decreased pulmonary blood flow, “boot” shaped heart, and right ventricular hypertrophy.

【71】 On cross-sectional imaging, the aberrant left subclavian artery can be seen coursing behind the trachea and the esophagus.

【25】**Case Study Analysis**

【26】The assessment on the patient is completed and data analysis is as follows： A 16-year-old female with an 8-day history of prolonged heavy menstrual flow and increased cramping that presents with a hematocrit level of 20. The patient had extreme tenderness on pelvic examination to include an enlarged uterus with the posterior part of uterus positive for ten-derness. When the cervix was palpated， the patient was noted to have discomfort. Fundal height of the uterus is measured at 4 cm. An enlarged uterus and cervical discomfort are not associated with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Abdominal pain and cramping are not associated with uterine fibroids. A urine pregnancy test done on the patient is positive. The diagnosis is threatened abortion. A referral to OB/GYN is made as well as counseling the patient on birth control methods for the future. A transvaginal ultrasound will most likely be completed during the OB/GYN appointment to confirm the diagnosis.

【28】**_Case Presentation： A 66-year-old African American woman reports a complaint of_ _hip pain from a fall she had 3 weeks ago._**

【29】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【30】Hip pain can occur from a fall and subsequent damage to the hip joint. Damage can also occur from a number of causes including sports-related injury exercises， old age， over-use， and falls. Also， certain diseases lead to hip pain， including osteoarthritis， rheumatoid arthritis， avascular arthritis， and bone cancer.

【31】**Injuries That Cause Hip Pain**

【32】**_Hip Dislocation_**

【33】· An injury to a joint in which the ends of the bones are forced from their normal positions

【34】**· This injury immobilizes the hip joint and results in sudden and severe pain**

【35】**_Hip Fracture_**

【36】·Usually occurs in the joint area where the head of the femur is fractured. This results in extreme pain and immobility

【37】· Multiple medications

【38】**_Hip Labral Tear_**

【39】**·Tear involves the labrum that follows the outside rim of the socket of the hip joint**

【40】· The labrum acts like a socket to hold the ball at the top of the femur in place

【41】**_Compartment Syndrome_**

【42】·Results from bleeding or swelling after an injury into a compartment space

【43】· High pressure in compartment syndrome impedes the flow of blood to and from the affected tissues

【44】**_Osteoporosis_**

【45】**·Causes bones to become weak and brittle so that a fall or even mild stresses， like bending over or coughing， can cause a fracture**

【46】·Physical findings include palpable tenderness over the area of compression fracture

【47】**·Osteoporosis-related fractures most commonly occur in the hip， wrist， or spine， espe-cially in older people**

【48】**Bursitis**

【49】**· Affects the bursae**

【50】·Occurs when bursae become inflamed and patient experiences pain

【51】**Tendinitis**

【52】**·Inflammation or irritation of a tendon**

【53】·Causes focal pain and tenderness just outside a joint due to trauma-related activities

【54】**· One of the most common sites is hip**

【55】**Diseases That Cause Hip Pain**

【56】**Osteoarthritis**

【57】**·Most common form of arthritis**

【58】**· Often called wear-and-tear arthritis**

【59】· Occurs when the protective cartilage on the ends of the bones wears down over time

【60】**Rheumatoid Arthritis**

【61】· Affects the synovial membranes， causing edema

【62】·Results in bone erosion and damage to ligaments and tendons

【63】**· An autoimmune disorder**

【64】**_Paget's Disease_**

【65】·Disrupts body's normal bone recycling process

【66】· Old bone tissue is gradually replaced with new bone tissue

【67】· Over time， the affected bones become fragile and can cause pain and tenderness

【11】**Red Flags**

【12】No improvement with physical therapy

【13】Progression of symptoms (pain went from “sore" to“burn-ing，" and intermittent to constant)

【14】Young age

【15】Clinical signs of all types of bursitis are similar and include local tenderness， warmth， and erythema. The latter two signs may not be obvious when the inflamed bursa is located deep beneath soft tissues or muscles， as in this case.10/

【16】The presence of a “lump”or swelling as presented in this case caused a delay in medical referral and diagnosis because MRI findings were consistent with a diagnosis of an inflammatory mass. In this case symptoms progressed and did not fit the typical pattern for bursitis (e.g.， pain at night， no position comfortable).

【17】**Other Tests**

【18】When a client is sent back a second time， the therapist's reevaluation is essential for documenting any changes from the original baseline and discharge findings. Reevaluation should include the following：

【19】Test for the sign of the buttock to look for serious disease posterior to the axis of flexion and extension of the hip . A positive sign may be an indication of abscess， fracture， neoplasm， septic bursitis， or osteomyelitis.删除14:<u>15</u>

【20】A noncapsular pattern is typical with bursitis and by itself is not a red flag. A capsular pattern with a diagnosis of bursitis would be more suspicious. Limited straight leg raise with no further hip flexion after bending the knee is a typical positive buttock sign seen with ischial bursitis. The absence of this sign would raise clinical suspicion that the diagnosis of bursitis was not accurate.删除14:<u>15</u>

【21】With an ischial bursitis， expect to see equal leg length， nega-tive Trendelenburg test， and normal sensation， reflexes， and joint play movements.108 Anything outside of these parameters should be considered a yellow (caution) flag.

【22】Assess for trigger points (TrPs) that may cause buttock pain， especially quadratus lumborum， gluteus maximus， and ham-strings， but also gluteus medius and piriformis.

【23】Ureteral pain usually begins posteriorly in the costoverte-bral angle but may radiate anteriorly to the upper thigh and groin ， or it may be felt just in the groin and genital area. These pain patterns represent the path-way that genitals take as they migrate during fetal devel-opment from their original position， where the kidneys are located in the adult， down the pathways of the ure-ters to their final location. Pain is referred to a site where the organ was located during fetal development. A kid-ney stone down the pathway of the ureters causes pain in the flank that radiates to the scrotum (male) or labia(female).

【24】The lower thoracic and upper lumbar vertebrae and the SI joint can refer pain to the groin and anterior thigh in the same pain pattern as occurs with renal disease. Irritation of the T10-L1 sensory nerve roots (genitofemoral and ilioingui-nal nerves) from any cause， especially from diskogenic dis-ease， may cause labial (women)， testicular (men)， or buttock pain.109 The therapist can evaluate these conditions by con-ducting a neurologic screening examination and using the screening model.

【25】Referred symptoms from ureteral colic can be distin-guished from musculoskeletal hip pain by the history， the presence of urologic symptoms， and the pattern of pain. Is there any history of urinary tract impairment? Is there a recent history of other infection? Are any signs and symp-toms noted that are associated with the renal system?

【26】Active TrPs along the upper rim of the pubis and the lateral half of the inguinal ligament may lie in the lower internal oblique muscle and possibly in the lower rectus abdominis. These TrPs can cause increased irritability and spasm of the detrusor and urinary sphincter muscles， pro-ducing urinary frequency， retention of urine， and groin pain.删除14:<u>65</u>

【27】The therapist can perform Murphy's percussion test to rule out kidney involvement . A positive Murphy's percussion test (pain is repro-duced with percussive vibration of the kidney) points to the possibility of kidney infection or inflammation. When this test is positive， ask about a recent history of fever， chills， unexplained perspiration (“sweats")， or other constitu-tional symptoms.

【28】**SCREENING FOR INFECTIOUS AND INFLAMMATORY CAUSES OF LOWER QUADRANT PAIN**

【29】Anyone with joint pain of unknown cause who presents with current or recent (i.e.， within the past 6 weeks) skin rash or recent history of infection (e.g.， hepatitis， mononucleosis， urinary tract infection， upper respiratory infection， sexually transmitted infection， streptococcus， dental infection)110，111must be referred to a health care clinic or medical doctor for further evaluation.

【30】Conditions affecting the entire peritoneal cavity such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) or appendicitis may cause hip or groin pain in the young， healthy adult. Widespread inflammation or infection may be well tolerated by athletes， sometimes for up to several weeks (Case Example 16.12).

【31】**Clinical Presentation**

【32】The clinical presentation can be deceptive in young people. The fever is not dramatic and may come and go. The ath-lete may dismiss excessive or unusual perspiration (“sweats") as part of a good workout. Loss of appetite associated with systemic disease is often welcomed by teenagers and young adults and is not recognized as a sign of physiologic distress.

【33】With an infectious or inflammatory process， laboratory tests may reveal an elevated ESR. Questions about the presence of any other symptoms may reveal constitutional symptoms such as elevated nocturnal temperature， sweats， and chills， suggestive of an inflammatory process (Case Example 16.13).

【34】**Psoas Abscess**

【35】Any infectious or inflammatory process affecting the abdom-inal or pelvic region can lead to psoas abscess and irritation of the psoas muscle. For example， lesions outside the ureter， such as infection， abscess， or tumor， or abdominal or peri-toneal inflammation， may cause pain with movement of the adjacent iliopsoas muscle that presents as hip or groin pain.

【36】PID is another common cause of pelvic， groin， or hip pain that can cause psoas abscess and a subsequent positive ilio-psoas or obturator test. In this case it is most likely a young woman with multiple sexual partners who has a known or unknown case of untreated Chlamydia.

【37】The psoas muscle is not separated from the abdominal or pelvic cavity. Fig. 8.3 shows how most of the viscera， includ-ing the kidneys， sigmoid colon， jejunum， appendix， pancreas， abdominal aorta， and ureter， lie adjacent to the psoas muscle. Therefore any infectious or inflammatory process  can seed itself to the psoas muscle by direct extension， resulting in a psoas abscess-a localized collection of pus.

【38】Hip pain associated with such an abscess may involve the medial aspect of the thigh and femoral triangle areas . Soft tissue abscess may cause pain and tenderness to palpation without movement. 【40】She described her symptoms as pain with hip flexion when shifting the gears in her car. Some dance moves involving hip flexion also reproduced the pain， but this was not consistent. The pain was described as "deep，"“aching，" and“sometimes sharp， sometimes dull.

【41】Past medical history was significant for Crohn's disease， but the client was having no gastrointestinal (Gl) symptoms at this time. During the examination， no evidence of abdominal trigger points (TrPs) or muscle involvement was found. The pain was not reproduced with superficial palpation of the abdominal muscles on the day of the initial examination.

【42】Intervention with stretching exercises did not change the clini-cal picture during the first week.

【51】Any blood in your urine or stools?

【52】Any tingling or numbness in the groin area?· Any trouble sleeping at night?

【57】Any blood in your stools? Change in color of your bowel movements?

【58】Any foods or smells you cannot tolerate?

In a woman of reproductive years， it may be important to take a gynecologic history：Have you been examined by a gynecologist since this problem started?

【67】**_Limp After Total Hip Arthroplasty_**

【68】**A 70-year-old man was referred to physical therapy by his doctor1 year after a right total hip replacement (THR) for osteoarthritis. The client reports that he is in good general health without pain. His primary problem is a persistent limp， despite completion of a THR rehabilitation protocol.**

【69】**How can you tell whether this is an infectious versus biomechanical problem?**

【3】### 29.3.2 Extracutaneous Findings

【4】Osteomas occur in approximately 20 % of patients with GS and favor the mandible and maxilla. Less frequently, they can develop in long bones or the skull and are commonly associated with cutaneous cysts 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 6 \]</u>. Osteomas can present as early as childhood and often predate intestinal polyposis. These tumors are benign and painless but may be multiple or grow to reach significant enough size to be detected on physical exam 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 \]</u>. Other skeletal abnormalities in GS include exostoses, endostoses, and cortical thickening of the long bones 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 \]</u>.

【5】Dental anomalies are well described in GS and are seen in approximately 20 % of patients. These include odontomas and odontogenic cysts; absent, supernumerary, or rudimentary teeth; and multiple dental caries 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 6 \]</u>.

【6】Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE) affects approximately two-thirds of patients with GS and can be an early sign of the syndrome 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>. CHRPE is a patch of darkly pigmented retinal epithelium that can be detected on ophthalmologic exam at birth 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 \]</u>. While unilateral solitary CHRPE is not specific for FAP, multiple or bilateral lesions are considered highly specific for FAP 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 6 , 15 \]</u>. In GS, CHRPE is associated with mutations between codons 767 and 1513 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 16 \]</u>.

【7】Importantly, patients with GS are at increased risk for the development of several extracolonic malignancies. These include duodenal cancer, papillary thyroid carcinoma (mostly in females), brain tumors (glioblastoma, astrocytoma, medulloblastoma), hepatoblastoma (mostly in children), pancreatic and biliary tract carcinomas, adrenal adenoma, and various sarcomas (including fibrosarcoma and osteosarcoma) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 5 , 6 , 11 , 17 \]</u>.

【8】### 29.3.3 Gastrointestinal Manifestations

【9】FAP is characterized by the development of hundreds of adenomatous polyps of the colorectum that typically appear in the second decade 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 \]</u>. These polyps invariably undergo malignant transformation resulting in colorectal carcinoma (CRC) at a mean age of 39 years if undetected or untreated 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 18 \]</u>. Polyps occur primarily in the colon (typically bilaterally, but may initially be right sided) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 \]</u>, but can also be found in the small intestine and stomach in over 50 % of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 \]</u>. Consideration of FAP or GS is often made when a patient presents with GI symptoms including bleeding, anemia, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, or weight loss.

【10】29.4 Work-Up
------------

【11】Patients suspected of having FAP/GS should be managed by a multidisciplinary medial team, including dermatologists, gastroenterologists, geneticists, and surgeons. The diagnosis of FAP should be suspected in any patient found to have multiple colorectal adenomas with any of the manifestations described above or in first-degree relatives of affected family members. In a patient who has cysts with an atypical histology, along with a history of jaw cysts, the diagnosis of GS should be considered. These may present prior to gastrointestinal signs in some patients.

【12】Genetic testing for APC mutations is required for a definitive diagnosis of FAP. Molecular testing for APC mutations is commercially available and recommended for all patients suspected of having FAP/GS and their first-degree relatives.

【13】Cutaneous cysts in patients with GS usually demonstrate the same microscopic changes as ordinary epidermoid cysts (lining of keratinizing epithelium including a granular layer containing loose lamellar keratin within the cyst) but also classically demonstrate cysts with pilomatrical differentiation (containing areas of ghost cell keratinization) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 19 \]</u>. “Gardner fibromas” appear as sheets of thick, haphazardly arranged collagen bundles with interspersed bland fibroblasts 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 20 \]</u>. Intestinal polyps of GS show adenomatous hyperplasia of the mucosa 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 21 \]</u>.

【14】29.5 Treatment
--------------

【15】Management of the extraintestinal and intestinal manifestations of GS necessitates involvement of a multidisciplinary medical team. Symptomatic epidermoid cysts can be managed by intralesional steroid injection or surgical excision 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u>. Desmoid tumors can be managed by surgical excision, though there is a high rate of recurrence and recurring tumors may be more aggressive 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 \]</u>. If wide surgical excision of desmoid tumors fails, hormonal therapy (e.g. tamoxifen, raloxifene), and/or anthracycline-containing chemotherapy can be tried 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 22 \]</u>. Some osteomas in GS may be amenable to surgical intervention 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 , 11 \]</u>. Medications that affect prostaglandin metabolism, such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, have been reported to reduce the risk of colorectal cancer and desmoids tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 23 \]</u>.

【16】Because of the significant risk of malignancy, strict screening regimens are crucial for patients with FAP/GS. Due to the inevitability of developing CRC, patients with FAP/GS should undergo annual sigmoidoscopy starting at age 10–15 and prophylactic colectomy is typically recommended when polyps are identified or by the end of the 2nd or 3rd decade 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 , 6 , 18 \]</u>. Chemoprevention with cyclooxygenase inhibitors (i.e. celecoxib) has been associated with some level of polyp regression, but is not adequate to control the cancer risk 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 24 \]</u>.

【17】Other recommended screening includes upper GI endoscopy every 1–3 years (depending on polyp burden) along with annual thyroid exam due to risk of malignancy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 18 , 25 \]</u>. Annual abdominal ultrasounds and monitoring of serum α-fetoprotein levels during the first 5 years of life are recommended due to risk of hepatoblastoma in this age group 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u>. Ophthalmologic exam should be performed upon consideration of the diagnosis of FAP/GS to evaluate for the presence of CHRPE. Panoramic dental radiographs can detect osteomas, odontomas, and supernumerary teeth, and long-bone x-rays can be used to detect osteomas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 \]</u>. No consensus exists for routine screening for the detection of desmoid tumors, but palpable masses or symptoms should be explored using computerized tomography 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u>.

【18】Genetic counseling is an extremely important consideration and all family members should be offered genetic testing and be evaluated for evidence of GS.

【19】29.6 Conclusion
---------------

【20】Gardner syndrome affects multiple body systems, including the skin, soft tissue, bone, gastrointestinal system, as well as other solid organs. Recognition of cutaneous signs may provide an early diagnosis and can be lifesaving with proper management.

【58】30.1 Introduction
-----------------

【59】Basal cell nevus syndrome (BCNS) is an autosomal dominantly inherited condition first described in 1960 by Dr. Gorlin and Dr. Goltz 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u>. BCNS is known by several other names including nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, basal cell carcinoma nevus syndrome, Gorlin syndrome, and Gorlin-Goltz syndrome. Although BCNS demonstrates a high degree of penetrance, the diagnosis can be challenging due to its variable expressivity even within families 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 3 \]</u> and the age-dependent appearance of certain traits associated with this disorder. Some of the more frequent and characteristic features of BCNS include multiple basal cell carcinomas (BCCs), odontogenic keratocysts, skeletal abnormalities, palmar and/or plantar pits, calcified falx cerebri, and facial dysmorphism 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u>. Other clinical features found in association with BCNS include neoplasms such as medulloblastoma, ovarian fibroma, and cardiac fibromas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 – 7 \]</u>.

【60】30.2 Background
---------------

【61】BCNS results from mutations in the PTCH1 tumor suppressor gene which is found on chromosome 9q22.3-q31 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 8 \]</u>. The product of the PTCH1 gene normally represses gene transcription in the Hedgehog signaling pathway by acting as a transmembrane receptor for the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) ligand 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>. The Hedgehog signaling pathway was first described as a developmental pathway during research on the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Post-developmentally in humans, the Hedgehog signaling pathway is typically only active in hair follicles and skin cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 \]</u>. The neoplasms of the syndrome require two hits to the PTCH1 gene, with a mutation in the second normal allele 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 12 \]</u>. However, some clinical features of BCNS, such as palmar pits, bifid rib, and macrocephaly, only require the inherited defective allele 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>.

【62】Women and men appear to be equally affected by BCNS. However, the prevalence of BCNS ranges from 1/57,000 to 1/256,000 depending on the studied population 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 , 14 \]</u>. It should be noted that certain clinical manifestations of BCNS, mainly BCCs, are less prevalent in darker skin individuals 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 15 \]</u>.

【63】30.3 Clinical Presentation
--------------------------

【64】More than 100 different clinical features have been found in association with BCNS 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 16 \]</u>. The most frequent and characteristic features of BCNS have been listed chronologically by age of presentation.

【65】Facial Dysmorphism : Most individuals with BCNS have one or more of the following “coarse” facial features: macrocephaly, frontal bossing, broad nasal bridge, prognathism, high arched eyebrows and/or palate, and cleft lip/palate 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 , 17 \]</u>. Patients with BCNS sometimes have a history of being delivered by cesarean section due to macrocephaly which is the most common facial dysmorphism associated with BCNS 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 18 \]</u>.

【66】Skeletal Abnormalities : In addition to abnormal skull findings, other skeletal abnormalities typically present at birth include bifid ribs, vertebral abnormalities, Sprengel shoulder, pectus deformity, short 4th metacarpal, and syndactyly of the digits 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 7 \]</u>.

【67】Ocular Abnormalities : Other congenital abnormalities associated with BCNS include severe eye defects such as strabismus, hypertelorism, telecanthus, cataracts, glaucoma, microphthalmia, orbital cyst, and coloboma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 , 14 , 17 \]</u>.

【68】Cardiac Fibromas : Less than 5 % of patients with BCNS develop cardiac fibromas which typically appear in the first year of life 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 \]</u>. 【25】**Granulomatous inflammation of the CNS**

【26】**· The majority of cases of CNS granulomatous diseases are infectious in etiology， especially tuberculosis， or represent sarcoidosis.**

【27】**· The distinction of tuberculous infection and sarcoidosis is of particular importance， especially from a therapeutic standpoint. However， the diagnosis of neurosarcoidosis is often difficult because of varied and nonspecific neurological manifestations. The leptomeninges are the most frequent site of CNS involvement by sarcoidosis， although it has a similar affinity to involve the base of brain as does tuberculous meningitis.**

【28】**· In general， granulomata are preferentially perivascular in location and are often associated with a chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate consisting of primarily Tlymphocytes，B lymphocytes， and monocytes. Granulomatous inflammatory disorders are characterized by the presence of multinucleated giant cells (epitheloid syncytial macrophages).**

【29】**·Common clinical manifestations of granulomatous disease include cranial neuropathies and/or obstructive hydrocephalus.**

【30】**1Mycobacterial infection**

【31】Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the most common cause.

【32】__ There are two major pathological manifestations in CNS tuberculosis： infec-tion involving the leptomeninges (with or without secondary ventriculitis) and inflammation confined to the parenchyma corresponding to a tubercu-loma (caseating granuloma).

【33】Posterior fossa tuberculoma may mimic a tumor.

【34】M. leprae causes leprosy. M. avium-intracellulare may cause meningitis in immunocompromised individuals.

【35】**2 Neurosarcoidosis**

【36】Histologically，sarcoidosis is characterized by non-caseating granulomas with large epithelioid cells and minimal necrosis. This is an important distinction from tuberculosis.

【37】__ Involvement of the central and peripheral nervous system in sarcoidosis oc-cur in approximately 5% of patients with this disease.

【38】 Of patients with nervous system involvement facial nerve palsy is the most common presenting cranial neuropathy. Cranial neuropathies are the most common neurological signs/symptoms (53%)， followed by parenchymal in-volvement (48%)， aseptic meningitis (22%)， peripheral neuropathy (17%)， myopathy (15%)， and hydrocephalus (7%).

【39】3Neurosyphilis

【40】Can produce meningovascular and parenchymatous involvement.

【41】__ Chronic leptomeningeal inflammation with spinal arachnoiditis and menin-geal thickening is not uncommon.

【42】4 Fungalinfections

【43】 For example， cryptococcosis， aspergillosis， coccidioidomycosis， and histo-plasmosis.

【44】__ Can produce meningitis as well as numerous cortical and subcortical micro-abscesses.

【45】5 Foreign body giant cell reaction

【46】 For example， suture materials， dermoid cyst rupture， history of traumatic brain injury， history of intravenous drugabuse.

【49】· The presence of small granulomas and giant cells in the setting of a pineal gland tumor should raise the suspicious of germinoma.

【50】7VWegener granulomatosis

【51】Histologically characterized by necrotizing granulomas and vasculitis affect-ing predominantly medium and small vessels.

【52】__ Neurological involvement occurs in 30% of patients and includes aseptic chronic meningitis. Mononeuritis multiplex is also common， seen in 15% of patients.

【53】__ Typical systemic pathological features include granulomatous lesions of the upper and lower respiratory tracts， focal segmental glomerulopathy， and necrotizing vasculitis， associated with symptoms related to upper and lower airways.

【63】**Heterotopias**

【64】**· A cortical heterotopia is characterized by islands of gray matter along the route of neuroblast migration. The islands consist of a collection of normal neurons in abnormal locations secondary to arrest of the radial migration of neuroblasts， no later than the fifth month of gestation.**

【65】**·The cause of incomplete migration is unknown.**

【66】**· They are associated with a wide variety of genetic， vascular， and environmental causes.**

【67】**Three types are recognized：**

【68】**1 Nodular (subependymal) heterotopia**

【69】·Subependymal masses of gray matter that form clusters of round nodules.

【70】 Usually localized at the corner of lateral ventricles.

【71】Normal development and mild symptoms with onset of seizures in the first two decades of life.

【72】2 Laminar (focal subcortical) heterotopia

【73】 Variable symptoms and signs depending on the extent of the heterotopia.

【74】·The larger the heterotopia， the more severe the developmental delay.

【75】3FBand heterotopia (double cortex)

【76】 Moderate to severe developmental delay and intractable seizures.

【77】**Neurofibrillary tangles**

【78】**·Neurofibrillary tangles are non-membrane bound masses of filaments， which are stained positive with silver stain.**

【79】**· The structures are composed of 10-20 nm filaments in paired helix configuration， crossover every 80 nm.**

【80】**· They are associated with phosphorylated tau protein (i.e.A68). Tau is a microtubule protein that promotes tubule stability and assembly.**

【81】Tangles are seen in a variety of pathologies including：

【82】**1 Alzheimer disease**

【83】Other pathologies include neuronal loss， neuritic plaques， and granulovacuo-lar degeneration. Hirano bodies and amyloid angiopathy can also be seen.

【84】__ Tangles are also seen in Down syndrome： by the age of 40 years， almost 100% of patients develop a pathology of Alzheimer disease but they can be asymptomatic.

【85】2 Normal aging

【86】**Exists in small numbers.**

【87】3 Progressive supranuclear palsy

After detailing the neuroepidemiology of HlV-l-associated cognitive/motor complex， we then describe the degrees of severity of neuropsychological impairment that are associat-ed with HIV-1 infection.**

【4】**The overall decrease in the incidence of AIDS is likely to be associated with a concurrent reduction in the incidence of HV-1-associated cogni-tive/motor complex， especially with respect to the more severe manifes-tations of the disorder. Because most of the epidemiological studies on HlV-l-associated cognitive/motor complex described below were con-ducted prior to the widespread use of combination antiretroviral thera-py， including protease inhibitors， these findings probably do not reflect the more recent epidemiologic trends. Additionally， because investiga-tions of HIV-1-associated neuropsychological impairment have been pri-marily conducted with MSMs and/or injection drug users， the results may not generalize to other groups， especially older adults. Therefore， the prevalence rates reported in these stadies should not necessarily be applied to current prevalence rates in this era of combination therapy**

【5】**Other limitations exist in the extant HIV-1 neuroepidemiologic data. For instance， there is less available data on the incidence of HIV1-associated neuropsychological impairment as prevalence rates are more often reported. The arrival of newer and more efficacious treatments will likely decrease the rate at which new cases of HIV-1-Associated Dementia (HAD) are identified， underscor-ing the need for adequate incidence data. Additionally， CDC nation-wide surveillance data report only the initial AIDS indicator condition； thus， subsequent conditions (i.e.， HIV encephalopathy) may not be recorded and the actual prevalence of this condition may be underesti-mated. Methodologic inconsistencies and confounds also partially account for the discrepant findings across studies. Changes in the tax-onomy used for disease classification  may also moderate prevalence rates. Another methodological consider ation is that not all studies reporting epideiniologic measurements of Hlv-i-associated cognitive/motor complex used neuropsychological testing to confirm impairment and guard against misdiagnosis， as rec-ommended by the American Academy of Neurology (AAN) task force on HIVI infection 通用删除7(英):<u>(1996)</u>. Mendez， van Gorp， and Cuminings 通用删除7(英):<u>(1995)</u> have cautioned against the sole use of clinical ratings of cognitive impair-ment because they are potentially inaccurate.**

【6】**Prevalence of HTV-1-Associated Dementia Complex**

【7】**The prevalence of neuropsychological impairment in seropositive indi-viduals varies as a function of disease stage. HAD is the most severe form of neuropsychological impairmert associated with the infection. HIV encephalopathy ， an earlier term for HAD， is the initial manifestation of AIDS in 2.8% of persons with the disease and has been estimated to have a prevalence of 7.3% in AIDS patients based on cases reported to the CDC . A retrospective chart review conducted in specialized HIV outpa-tient clinics at four New York City hospitals found the prevalence ofHTV encephalopathy to be 4.6% among individuals with AIDS . Using a prospective cohort study (Multicenter Aids Cohort Study-MAGS)， MacArthur et al. 通用删除7(英):<u>(1993)</u> reported that HAD is the ini-tial AIDS indicator illness in 3.3% of patients， a figure that is generally consistent with CDC data. The MACS data revealed that the annual inci-dence of HAD was 7% during the two years following an AIDS diagnosis and estimated that one year following the initial AIDS diagnosis， 7.1%of patients will have dementia. However， with the introduction of triple combination therapy， the annual incidence of HAD has been reported to be 1% . The cumulative incidence of dementia in a cohort of 492 AIDS patients from the MACS (Baltimore/Los Angeles site) was 15% over a seven-year period. Day and colleagues 通用删除7(英):<u>(1992)</u> reported a 28% cumulative incidence rate of dementia over 24 months in a much smaller group (N=32) of symptomatic seropositives and an annual incidence rate of 14%. Without an AIDS diagnosis， the preva-lence of HAD is minimat. During the asymptomatic stage of the disease，1987 CDC Stage II & III， the prevalence of HAD is 0.4% .**

【8】**Prevalence estimates of HAD from cross-cultural studies are consis-tent with prevalence rates obtained in samples fron the United States. Using a neuropsychological test battery developed for the World Health Organization's Neuropsychiatric AIDS Study and validated for cross-cultural use， Maj and colleagues 通用删除7(英):<u>(1994)</u> reported the prevalence of HAD amnong HIV-seropositives to be 4.4% to 6.9% across subjects evalu-ated in five centers (Germany， Brazil， Zaire， Kenya， and Thailand). Chiesi and associates 通用删除7(英):<u>(1996)</u> retrospectively reviewed medical charts and found the prevalence of HAD to be 4.5% at AIDS diagnosis across17 countries in Europe.**

【9】**Prevalence of Minor Cognitive Motor Disorder**

【10】**Minor cognitive motor disorder (MCMD) is a less severe manifestation of HlV-l-associated neuropsychological impairment. Both MCMD and subclinical， mild impairment in cognitive-motor functioning are far more prevalent than HAD . MCMD is most often associated with symptomatic (1993 CDC Stage B) or AIDS indicator conditions (1993 CDC Stage C) . As the disease progresses， the prevalence of cognitive motor impairment increases. For instance， across 13 studies of the neuropsychological effects of HIV l conducted between 1987 and 1995  the medi-an prevalence of cognitive motor impairment was 55% among AJDS patients in comparison to seronegative controls . The rate of neuropsychological impairment in symptomatic seroposi-tives (1993 CDC Category B) is lower； for example， Heaton and col-leagues 通用删除7(英):<u>(1995)</u> reported 44% of study participants were impaired based on clinical ratings.**

**In comparison to symptomatic HIVseropositive individuals， it has been even more difficult to estimate the prevalence of cognitive-motor impairment among asymptoniatic individuals because of the variability in findings across studies . Predictably， methodological issues have been critical to under-standing differences in reported prevalence rates of neuropsychologi-cal impairment in asymptomatic seropositive (ASP) patients. A review of' mostly cross-sectional studies (N = 57) examining mild cognitive-motor impairment in ASP individuals has provided some insight into the nature and degree of impairment in this group. Almost all of the studies (55/57) in the White and colleagues 通用删除7(英):<u>(1995)</u> review used the1987 CDC criteria to classify asymnptomatic HIV (i.e.， CDC Stage II or l). Stage II signifies a fully asymptomatic medical state， and Stage 1I includes persistent generalized lymphadenopathy. This classification revealed a median prevalence rate of 35% of neuropsychological impairinent for ASP persons versus 12% in seronegative (SN) con-trols--almost a three-fold difference. Classitication rates other than median prevalence may yield different findings. Additionally， evalua-tion of the length and comprehensiveness of the neuropsychological assessment revealed that extensive test batteries (more than 14 tests) were approximately three times more likely to find an increased rate of|删除0换行|neuropsychological impairment in ASP patients than studies using fewer than 14 tests. Mode of infection (i.e.， MSM， IVDU， blood trans-fusion，unknown) was also identified as a possible contributor to neu-ropsychological impairment. However， differences in findings were less conclusive due to the methodology and neuropsychological bat-teries used.**

【12】**It is noteworthy that the findings froin the MACS， which studied gay and bisexual men in the most comprehensive assessinent of the neuro-psychological consequerces of HTV-1 infection， revealed that neuropsy-chological deficits are not likely to be seen in ASP individuals when using standard neuropsychological measures . For example， the Miller group 通用删除7(英):<u>(1990)</u> examined769 HIV-seronegative controls with 727 HIV-seropositive ASPs from the MACS study， and found that performance did not differ between groups on any measure. Moreover， only 5.5% of the ASPs in that study showed abnormal performance on individual tests (i.e.， lwo standard deviations below mean for age-and education-matched controls).**

【13】**NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL DOMAINS DIFFERENTIALLY AFFECTED IN HIV-1-ASSOCIATED COGNITIVE/MOTOR COMPLEX**

【14】**Since the onset of Htv-1 infection， a numher of different terms have been employed to describe the neuropsychological consequences of this disease. For the purposes of this chapter， we will rely on the nomen-clature delineated by the American Academy of Neurology 通用删除7(英):<u>(1991)</u>.**

【15】**HIV-1-associated cognitive/motor complex is a term that subsumes minor cognitive motor disorder (MCMD) and HIV-associated dementia complex. Table 9.1 illustrates the preserved and impaired areas in each of these disorders. Psychomotor speed， complex reaction time， motoric functions， and working mnemory have been found to be affected in each of thesc manifestations of HIV1-associated cognitive/motor disorder. While divided attention and verbal fluency may be compromised in the subclinical presentation or MCMD， impairment in these areas generally occurs in HAD. Concentration， simple reaction time， executive func-tion， and memory may be impaired in MCMD and are also likely to be affected in HAD. Performance on relatively simple tasks of attention and language are generally preserved until the end stages. Emotionai disturbance (depression) is common in HIV-1 and may be the result of a psychological reactionto the infection； alternatively， behavioral**

【21】**SELECTINGANEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TEST BATTERY**

【22】**Cultural Status**

【23】**In the section detailing changes in the incidence and prevalence of HIV-1 infection， we emphasized that the demographic profile of indi-viduals with HlV infection in the United States has broadened to include individuals whose primary language is not English and/or whose cultural background is tot American. Sensitivity to demographic factors (i.e.， English language fluency and low education) that might affect individu-als' performance on various neuropsychological measures is particular-ly important. Therefore， in each of the neuropsychological domains listed below， we have included tests in which performance is less likely to be constrained by language and cultural factors.**

【24】**Mental Status**

【25】**Measures of basic cognitive functioning have been found to be limited in their ability to detect early signs of HlV-associated cognitive/motor complex . For instance， measures like the Mini-Mental Status Examination  and the Mattis Dementia Rating Scale  are less sensitive to HAD because they primarily assess symptoms typically found in cortical dementia (i.e.， language impairment， visuospatial deficits) rather than subcortical processes(L.e.， psychomotor speed， working meinory). Among the mental status screening instrumerts， the Mini-Mental Status Examination has been found to be useful only after patients reach the moderate stage of HAD and score below the suggested cutoff score .**

**The HIV Dementia Scale  is a screening instrument designed to assess psychomotor speed， concentration， and memory-areas that are often impaired in HAD. The HDS consists of four subtests： timed written alphabet，recall of four items at five minttes， cube copy time， and antisaceadic errors. The HDS was found to identify HAD with a greater sensitivity， positive predictive value， efficiency， and fikelihood ratio than the MMSE (Power et al.). The emphasis on timed tasks makes the HDS superior to the MMSE when assessing patients suspected of having HAD. While the diagnostic efficiency of the HDS is comparable to the Grooved Pegboard test， it is not dependent on instrumnentation (the pegboard) and is less affected|删除0换行|by peripheral neuropathy. Limitations of the HDS include the lack of information about its utility among individuals who are non-English speaking or are from other cultures. Moreover， the HDS may be less sensitive to detecting mild dementia in highly educated patients.**

【27】**Intelligence**

【28】**Overall intellectual functioning is affected by HIV-1 infection ， partially because a subset of the tests is sen-sitive to psychomotor speed. On four of the five subteses that comprise the Performance IQ. higher scores are partially contingent on speed of completion. Digit Symbol (from the Wcehsler Adult Intelligence Scale-Revised； WAIS-R) has been found to be the most sensitive of the WAIS-R subtests to the effects of HIV-1 infection . It is expected that deficits on Digit Symbol-Coding (from the WAIS-Hl) will be similar or even more pronounced since the length of this subtest was increased with the updating of the WAIS. With the addition of Symbol Search (WAIS-III) to the Performance subtests， a Processing Speed Index can be calculat-ed based on Symbol Search and Digit Symbol-Coding. The Processing Speed Index provides the ability to assess psychomotor speed relative to overall IQ and thus evaluate whether psychomotor slowing is present. With the changing demographics of the HIV1 epidemic， it is recom-mended that for semi-fluent and non-English speaking individuals， non-verbal measures of overall intellectual functioning be used. The Raven’s Progressive Matrices test is considered a more culture-fair test of intelli-gence than the WAIS-R  and mea-sures reasoning ability. Matrix Reasoning， an addition to the WAIS-II， may be a possible substitute for Raven’s Progressive Matrices as the wo tests are conceptually similar， though the convergent validity of these measures has not been tested.**

**HIV1-infected patients usually perform beter on the verbal subtests of the WAIS-R， which， except for Arithmetic， are not timed. However， it is common for patients to have difficulty on the digits backward portion of the Digit Span subtest because of working memory difficulties. With the WAISIlI， a potentially more sophisticated test of working memory func-tion was introduced---Letier-Number Sequencing. This subtest has been validated as a working memory task in individuals diagnosed with|删除0换行|schizophrenia (Gold， Carpenter， Randolph， Goldberg， & Weinberger1997)， and it is likely to be sensitive to assessing deficits affected in HIV1. While the WAIS-Il allows for the calculation ofa Working Memory Index(based on Digit Span， Arithmetic， and Letter-Number Sequencing)， this Index is composed of an amalgam of tasks. For instance， Digits Forward is not considered to be a measure of working memory and it is unclear whether Arithmetic is actually an index of working memory. Therefore， the Working Memory Index may well be useful as a preliminary screen of working memory function that should be followed up with other tests when impairment or lower-than-expected performance is detected.**

【30】**Language**

【31】**Language functions are rarely affected in HIV-1  unless the patient has a focal CNS OI or a CNS tumor affecting the language areas of the brain. On measures of verbal fluency ， the performance of HIV-1-infected individuals has been variable . Deficient fluency can be due to problems other than language impairment， including frontal lobe impairment and psychomotor siow-ing . Speech may be slow due to psychomotor slowing. Dysarthria (slurring of speech) and hypophonia (decreased volume) rarely occur in HAD. Similarly， because of motor difficulties， penmanship may deteriorate. Finally， HIV-l-infected individuals may complain of reading difficulties； however， these are most frequently due to concentration problems rather than alexia.**

【44】**LOWBACKPAIN**

【45】**_Case Presentation： A 35-year-old male painter presents to your clinic with the complaint oflow back pain. He_ _recalls lifting a 5-gallon paint can and felt an immediate pull in the lower right side of his back. This happened2 days ago and he bad the weekend to rest， but after taking Motrin and using beat， be has not seen any_ _improvement. He is having some right leg pain but no bowel or bladder changes. His pain is sharp， stabbing，_ _and he scored it as a 9 on a scale of0 to 10. He had a similar incident approximately 5 years ago but made a_ _complete recovery._**

【46】**INTRODUCTIONTO COMPLAINT**

【47】Acute low back pain is a common problem seen in primary care practices. Most low back pain can affects approximately 80% of the population between the ages of 25 and 45 years. Fortunately， 90% of back injuries are benign and account for the fifth most common visit in primary care. Some of the important characteristics of low back pain that are critical to making the correct diagnosis are：

【48】·Localized pain that is worse with moving due to muscle pain

【49】**·Trauma may cause a fracture and requires an x-ray**

【50】·Radiating pain into the leg along a dermatone indicates a ruptured disc

【51】**·Loss of bowel or bladder function indications an emergency**

【52】**· Back pain that is continuous and associated with a history of cancer requires diagnostic testing to rule out malignancy**

【13】#### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations

【14】In general, many apocrine DCIS cases show a mixture of histologic patterns and cytologic types. These do not appear to have a major biologic significance, so recognition of DCIS is more important than subcategorisation as apocrine DCIS. Treatment and prognosis depend mainly on other factors such as size, extent, margin status, and biomarker expression.

【15】### Invasive Apocrine Carcinoma

【16】#### Definition

【17】Invasive apocrine carcinoma has generally been regarded as a morphologic variant of invasive breast carcinoma not otherwise specified, rather than a special type of invasive cancer 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 32 – 36 \]</u>.

【18】#### Clinical and Epidemiological Features

【19】Invasive apocrine carcinomas of the breast are not clinically distinct from invasive carcinoma not otherwise specified. The reported incidence of apocrine carcinoma varies from <0.5 to 4 % in the literature 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 , 16 , 17 , 32 – 37 \]</u>. This variability in incidence is most likely due to the lack of well-defined diagnostic criteria to define apocrine carcinoma. In general, it is recommended that the term should be reserved for neoplasms in which almost all tumour cells show apocrine cytological features. In contrast, focal apocrine differentiation is quite common and has been reported in up to 60 % of invasive carcinomas of no special type.

【20】When the diagnosis of apocrine carcinoma is based on the immunohistochemical expression of GCDFP-15, the incidence of apocrine carcinoma has been as high as 70 % 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 16 , 17 \]</u>. Areas of apocrine differentiation have also been reported in other special types of invasive breast cancers, such as invasive papillary and lobular carcinomas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 16 , 17 \]</u>.

【21】#### Imaging Features

【22】Tumour size, presentation, incidence of lymph node positivity, and imaging findings of apocrine carcinomas do not differ significantly from invasive carcinomas of no specific type 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 38 , 39 \]</u>.

【23】#### Pathologic Features

【24】##### Macroscopic Pathology

【25】There are no distinct findings associated with apocrine carcinoma. Invasive apocrine carcinomas are grossly indistinguishable from other invasive breast carcinomas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 34 – 37 \]</u>.

【26】##### Microscopic Pathology

【27】Microscopically, apocrine carcinomas show growth patterns similar to invasive carcinomas not otherwise specified. The only distinct feature is the cytological appearance. The cells typically have apocrine morphology with abundant granular cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei with prominent, often multiple, nucleoli . The grade of the lesion can be low (grade 1), intermediate (grade 2), or high (grade 3). Necrosis and abundant mitoses are common in high-grade lesions  通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 32 – 37 \]</u>. Most apocrine carcinomas are of the ductal type, but lobular carcinomas (especially pleomorphic lobular carcinomas) may show apocrine cytologic features. At the ultrastructural level, apocrine carcinomas have abundant intracytoplasmic organelles including secretory granules, mitochondria, and incomplete cristae 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 16 , 17 \]</u>.

【47】#### Differential Diagnosis

【48】##### Breast Neoplasms with Abundant Cytoplasm

【49】Abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm is a hallmark of cells of apocrine lesions. Many other epithelial and mesenchymal lesions of the breast may have abundant cytoplasm owing to accumulation of mitochondria, lysosomes, secretory granules, glycogen, or fat and thus may mimic apocrine carcinoma. These lesions include granular cell tumour and histiocytoid, lipid-rich, and secretory carcinomas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 51 \]</u>. Breast carcinomas with squamous differentiation or metastatic carcinomas also may have similar features mimicking apocrine breast cancer.

【50】Granular cell tumours are characterised by a proliferation of cells with abundant, coarsely granular cytoplasm. In appearance, the cytoplasm and granules can be basophilic, in contrast to the eosinophilia of apocrine carcinoma . Granular cell tumour nuclei are small and typically do not have prominent nucleoli, which are commonly seen in apocrine carcinomas. Immunohistochemical staining for cytokeratins (negative) and S100 (positive) is helpful in this diagnosis.

【4】**THE STRUCTURE OF COGNITIVE ABILITY：INTRAINDIVIDUALVARIABILITY**

【5】**In a monumental piece of work， Carroll 通用删除7(英):<u>(1993)</u> reanalyzed 460 data sets of performance on a wide variety of cognitive tasks. His findings sup-ported a hierarchical model of higher-order abilities. There is abundant evidence to support a factor of general intelligence (stratum II， com-monly called g) that permeates to some degree all cognitive tasks. However， at a lower-order level of analysis (called stratum II)， Carroll found strong support for eight broad ability factors. These include fac-tors that are familiar to neuropsychologists， such as fluid intelligence， crystallized intelligence， general memory ability， and cognitive speed. At the lowest level of analysis (stratum I) are many very specific abilities. For example (and related to the stratum II general memory ability factor) are specific abilities such as associative memory learning， and free recall.**

**CarrolI’s work provides a mnodel for discussion of a major problem with current methods of prediction of premorbid cognitive ability. In practice， estimation methods reflect the assumption that there is a sin-gle estimate (in practice， this is usually the estimated premorbid Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale FSIQ  that best rep-resents an individual's cognitive abilities. Thus， a common prediction statement in a neuropsychological report is “the patient’s premorbid level of cognitive ability is estimated to have been in the Average range.”Such statements are essentially a comment on g or general intelligence， In neuropsychological assessment， however， our interests lie not only in determining decline in g， but also in assessing decline in cognitive domains (e.g.， language， visuospatial ability， memory， executive func-tions) and specific abilities (e.g.， language comprehension， language expression， visual recognition， short-term auditory memory). Thus， our interests are in all three strata， not just in g. Current approaches to premorbid estimation generally ignore intraindividual scatter， or vary ing levels of ability， across and within the domains in which we are inter ested because they focus primarily on FSIQ-an approximate measure|删除0换行|of g . To use predictors of gas estimates of both specific stratum I abilities and general stratum II cognitive domains will inevitably result in incorrect estimates for some unknown number of comparisons during a neuropsychological evaluation. Straturn II domains are differentially related to g (i.e.， they do not correlate perfectly) and the stratum I abilities are differentially related to both gand the stratum II domains (i.e.， they have unique sources of variance).**

【21】**Historical Approaches**

【22】**_Previous Standardized Test Results_**

【23】**The ideal situation in clinical neuropsychological practice would be to have available for comparative purposes the results of a standardized multidimensional intelligence test (e.g.， WISC-R， WISC-III， WAIS-R) completed at some point prior to the onset not only of the suspected neurological disorder， but also of common disorders of adulthood such as hypertension. Although prior IQ test results are rarely available， the results of standardized aptitude or achievement testing can be obtained frequently in the United States. Nationally standardized assessment is completed within the educational system at a variety of points in time， beginning in the elementary grades (e.g.， the Stanford Achievement Tests) and extending through college and postgraduate levels (e.g.， Scholastic Aptitude Test， Graduate Record Exam). Because many of these standardized aptitude tests address multiple domains of cognitive function， they can provide the clinician with more specific estimates across different cognitive domains. Thus， standardized tests with mea-sures of verbat， mathematical/quantitative， and logical/analytic abilities permit more detailed comparisons with results from the neuropsycholog-ical evaluation. Finally， military entrance exams (ASVAB) may be another source of information regarding premorbid cognitive functioning.**

【24】**Use of prior test data can have several shortcomings， however. A prac-tical but frequent difficulty is that obtaining results of prior standard-ized tests can be time consuming and can delay substantially the completion of the neuropsychological consultation report. For this rea son， such data are typically obtained only in forensic cases. Few hospital-based consultation practices attempt to obtain such information for the routine case， in which turnaround for the completed report is mea-sured in hours or days.**

**Another significant problem is that scores on different standardized tests reflect different reference groups and the relationship between these groups and the normative reference groups for different neu-ropsychological tests is usually unknown. For example， the normative|删除0换行|group for standardized tests administered in the educational system becomes progressively stratified. Standardized tests completed during elementary and secondary school (not including college admission tests) likely reflect the population at large (similar to the normative ref-erence group for Wechsler’s intelligence and memory scales). However， fewer individuals take more advanced measures， such as college apti-tude tests. The normative base therefore becomes smaller and generally consists of a more homogeneous sample of individuals with higher levels of ability. Thus， measures of central tendency will increase (e.g.， mean performance) while measures of dispersion will decrease (e.g.， standard deviations). For example， an overall score at the 50th percentile on the GRE is likely to be roughly equivalent to a percentile score of 85 on apti-tude tests completed in high school (e.g.， on the SAT). It is much more difficult to estimate the IQ equivalent scores for the tails of the distribu-tion on different aptitude tests because of differences in both means and standard deviations across measures.**

【27】**In the absence of standardized test results， other aspects of a patient's history can be used to provide estimates of premorbid level(s) of func-tioning. 【20】**KEY FACTS**

【21】**_CLINICAL_**

【22】**PPostprimary TB is rare in children who were infected before 2 years of age. This entity is most commonly seen when initial infection was in adolescence.**

【23】**Postprimary TB in the lungs can produce fibroreticular or fibronodular opacities in the upper lobes. Superior retraction of the hila， fibrosis of the upper lobes， trac tion bronchicctasis， volume loss， and focal calcification can result. Cavitation and apical pleural thickening can also be seen. Lymphadenopathy is rare in children with postprimary TB.**

【24】**In children， similar chest radiographic appearances can be seen with histoplasmosis and atypical mycobacterial infections. Cystic fibrosis can have a similar appearance and distribution but increased lung volumes would be expected.**

【25】**_Gastrointestinal TB in industrialized countries is cur-_ rently most commonly due to Mycobacterium tubercu-losis. As a result of improved milk hygiene， M. bovis as a gastrointestinal pathogen has been largely controlled.**

【26】**The most common sites of tuberculous involvement of the gastrointestinal tract arc the ileocecal region and the ascending colon.**

【27】**The clinical symptoms of patients with colonic TB arc nonspecific and include diarrhea， abdominal pain， weight loss， and fever.**

【28】**Colonic TB is commonly seen with either concurrent or prior pulmonary TB， but pulmonary TB need not be present.**

【29】**Diagnosis of gastrointestinal TB depends on biopsy or scgmental resection， because stool examination， cul-tures， and colonoscopic examinations are frequently nondiagnostic.**

【30】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【31】**Radiographic findings in children with postprimary pulmonary TB are similar to those seen in adults(postprimary infections are rare in children with nor-mal immune systems) and primarily include a hetero-geneous (sometimes cavitary) opacity in the upper lobes. Severe fibrosis can lead to upper lobe volume loss， hilar retraction， and secondary tracheomegaly Pleural thickening is also common.**

【32】**Caseous necrosis occurs more often in the mesenteric lymph nodes than the bowel wall. Low attenuation lymph nodes， however， are not unique to TB and can also be found with gonadal metastases， atypical mycobacteria， and lymphoma.**

【33】**TB involvement of the colon is evident by mucosal ulceration and nodularity， mural rigidity， luminal nar-rowing， and fistulae. Involvement can be scgmental. Occasionally， an intraluminal mass can be identified.**

【46】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【47】**Ovarian teratoma： Any tumorous growth from the ovary could grow to the size shown in this case. How-ever， extension around the sacrum is not a feature typi-cally seen in ovarian tumor， making this an unlikely diagnosis.**

【48】**Abscess： This entity cannot be excluded on the basis of imaging findings alone. However， it is an unlikely diagnosis because the clinical history does not suggest the presence of infectious process.**

【49】**Neuroblastoma (or ganglioneuroma)： The location and appearance of the mass are consistent with this diagnosis. However， posterior encasement and direct sacral involvement are not findings that would be expected in pelvic neuroblastoma.**

【50】**Sacrococcygeal germ cell tumor (i.e.， teratoma)：Teratoma is the best diagnosis， based on the presacral and retrorectal location and， in particular， the encase-ment of sacral scgments.**

【51】**Anterior meningocele： This diagnosis is unlikely because the mass is not cystic.**

【52】**Rhabdomyosarcoma： Because posterior sacral exten-sion would be unusual for rhabdomyosarcoma， this is an unlikcly diagnosis.**

【53】**Primary bone tumor： A primary bone tumor is not a likely consideration because there is no bony destruction and sacral involvement in this case is relatively minimal.**

【54】**Gastrointestinal duplication： This diagnosis is unlikely because rectal duplications are very rare and extension to sacrum would not be expected.**

【55】**DIAGNOSIS： Malignant sacrococcygeal germ cell tumor (teratoma).**

【56】** KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【57】**Sacrococcygeal teratomas are relatively rare， with an estimated prevalence of l in 35，000-40，000 births.**

【58】**The category of germ cell tumors includes teratomas， choriocarcinomas， embryonal cell carcinomas， yolk sac tumors， and mixed types.**

【59】** Teratomas are classified as mature， immature， or malig-nant. Malignancy is rare in mature types.**

【60】**Treatment consists of chemotherapy and surgical resection.**

【61】**__ Early diagnosis and surgical excision is indicated because the incidence of malignant transformation increases with advancing age.**

【62】**Four types of sacral teratomas have been described， according to the internal and external components of the mass：**

【63】**Type 1： primarily external to the pelvis**

【64】**Type 2： predominantly external to the pelvis with intrapelvic component**

【65】**Type 3： primarily intrapelvic with only a small extrapelvic portion**

【66】**Type 4： entirely presacral without extrapelvic extension**

【67】**In general， the greater the intrapelvic component， the greatcr the likelihood of malignancy.**

【68】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【69】**Calcification is visible by CT in 50% to 60% of sacro-coccygeal teratomas and is more frequent in benign lesions. Amorphous， chunky， punctate， and spiculated calcifications have all been described.**

【70】**Cystic and fatty components can also be seen within the mass.**

【71】**Primarily solid lesions are more likely to be malignant. However， the histologic features (i.e.， benign or malig nant nature) cannot generally be inferred reliably from the imaging characteristics.**

【72】**__ LDirect invasion of adjacent structures suggests malig nant transformation.**

【73】**Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein levels are often pre-sent and are frequently followed in conjunction with imaging findings as a measure of tumor response.**

【74】**Presacral masses can coexist with two other entities：anorectal malformations and sacral anomalies， a con-stellation that is referred to as Currarino's triad.**

【125】**\*KEY FACTS**

【126】**_CINICAL_**

【127】**Almost all pulmonary masses in children are related to infection (e.g.， round pneumonia， plasma cell granuloma).**

【128】**Round pneumonia is a common cause of pulmonary mass in children.**

【129】**Round pneumonia is rare over 8 years of age.**

【130】**_Streptocoeeus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) is the most_ common organism responsible for round pneumonia.**

【131】**Symptoms can be mild or nonspecific early in the clini-cal course，**

【132】**With a typical clinical history and recognition of a mass on imaging studies as round pneumonia， antibi-otic treatment can be started without further imaging.**

【133】**In cases in which the clinical information is unclear， a pulmonary mass can be conservatively followed with a repeat chest radiograph in 24 to 48 hours. Round pneumonia will typically become closer in appearance to a lobar pneumonia at that time.**

【134】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【135】**Round pneumonia is typically a well-defined， mass-like opacity that is usually located in a lower lobe.**

【136】**Air bronchograms are present initially in a minority of cases.**

【137】**Calcification is not a feature of this entity.**

【138】**Pneumonia is initially localized due to immature collat-eral pathways in children， but eventually becomes a more typical air space disease process (i.e.，an ill-defined opacity with air bronchograms).**

【139】**__ Adenopathy and pleural effusion are rarely seen with round pneumonia.**

【35】**CONTROL OF HAIR COLOUR**

【36】Hair colour is under close genetic control； however， the exact hormonal and cellular mechanisms controlling melanocyte function are not clearly worked out. An intimate relationship must exist between the factors controlling melanocyte and matrix cell activity since melanocyte mitosis and melanosome production and transfer occur only during the anagen phase of the hair cycle. A negative feedback system has been postulated. Enzyme degradation products of melanosomes within matrix cells may cross cell membranes to melanocytes and control further melanin production or transfer. A melanocyte-specific ‘chalone’ acting within a negative feedback system may well exist for follicular melanocytes.

【37】**Follicular melanocytesareknownto respondlike epidermalmelanocytes to melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH)， which can darken light-coloured hair. Three forms of MSH have been described： these are small peptide hormones consisting of 12-18 amino acids. In vertebrates they are produced from the intermediate lobe of the pituitary gland. All three melanotrophins are cleavage products of a common precursor peptide， pro-opiomelanocortin. Corticotropin (adrenocorticotrophic hormone， ACTH) and o-MSH contain homologous internal sequences. Thus， the hyperpigmentation that occurs in Addison’s disease， Nelson’s syndrome and ectopic ACTH syndrome may be the result of ACTH， 0-MSH and even other peptides with common sequences. The effects of hormones other than MSH on hair pigmentation have yet to be elucidated. Oestrogens and progestogens may increase hair colour in view of their effect on the epidermis during pregnancy.**
